response.sql: WITH rental_totals AS (SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_paid FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN payment p ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id), store_avg AS (SELECT store_id, AVG(total_paid) AS avg_total FROM rental_totals GROUP BY store_id) SELECT rt.store_id, SUM(rt.total_paid) AS total_paid_sum, AVG(rt.total_paid - sa.avg_total) AS avg_excess FROM rental_totals rt JOIN store_avg sa ON sa.store_id = rt.store_id WHERE rt.total_paid > sa.avg_total GROUP BY rt.store_id ORDER BY rt.store_id;

assumptions.assumption: Store is taken from the rented inventory copy (rental.inventory_id -> inventory.store_id), as the request specifies.
Only payments with a non-NULL rental_id count; each rental's total is the sum of its linked payments.
Rentals with no linked payments have no payment total, so they are excluded from the store averages (the inner join matches 'averages ignore missing values').

The store-specific average is the mean of rental payment totals over that store's rentals only, and the 'average amount by which they exceed' is the mean of (rental total minus store average) over the qualifying rentals.
Amounts are returned unrounded, as the request asks.
